open_points.subject: Activation after trial-corpus growth
open_points.text: “The current activation of a contract version is the one recorded last” and activation “requires an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus,” but adding a trial case grows the corpus without defining what happens to an existing activation admitted over the former corpus.
open_points.question: When a trial case is added, does the existing activation remain current and runnable, become unusable, or cause the active implementation to be admitted again automatically?
options: Keep the existing activation current and runnable until another activation is recorded
Keep the activation record but refuse new runs until its implementation is admitted over the enlarged corpus
Automatically admit the active implementation over the enlarged corpus and retain or replace the activation according to the verdict
open_points.default_guess: Keep the existing activation current and runnable, because adding a case is not stated to create, remove or replace an activation.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity
open_points.text: M17 says “proving the same version gives the same result,” while the carried question says a version whose proof failed because a binding was not accepted “can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).” Accepting that binding can change the proof result without changing the flow version.
open_points.question: Is a ProofResult determined by the flow version alone, or is it a contextual result that may change as referenced bindings change status?
options: It is contextual and may differ when the same flow version is proved again
It is fixed for a flow version, so binding acceptance cannot change it
A binding-state snapshot is part of the ProofResult identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a contextual computed value that may change when a referenced binding is accepted.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution file outputs
open_points.text: K-14 says “Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`,” and M21 says a trial execution's output receives a class, but M07 says a file output stores “only its facts — digest, size and media type” and lists no disclosure class.
open_points.question: Does each file output recorded by TrialExecution carry a disclosure class, and if so is it stored directly or derived from the trial case inputs?
options: Store the derived disclosure class with each file-output fact
Derive the class when read from the trial case inputs and do not store it
Treat trial file outputs as exempt from the rule that every value carries a class
open_points.default_guess: Store the highest disclosure class among the execution's inputs with each file-output fact.

open_points.subject: Try implementation action
open_points.text: The action promises “trial evidence per case,” while M07 represents one implementation-and-case execution; the text never says which cases one `try an implementation` request executes.
open_points.question: Does the try action execute one named trial case, a caller-selected set of existing cases, or the whole current corpus?
options: A caller-selected nonempty set of existing trial cases
Every case in the contract version's current corpus
open_points.default_guess: Execute every case in the current corpus.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution actor provenance
open_points.text: K-15 says “The owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record,” but TrialExecution has no requester or cause even though records are created both by an agent's `try` action and by the kernel during admission.
open_points.question: What fact distinguishes a TrialExecution requested by a particular agent from one created automatically as part of admission?
options: Record the requesting actor and whether the cause was `try` or `admission` on TrialExecution
Introduce a parent trial/admission action record carrying the actor and cause
Treat every TrialExecution as a kernel action and do not retain the requesting agent or cause
open_points.default_guess: Record the requesting actor and the `try` or `admission` cause on each TrialExecution.

open_points.subject: Run completion with guarded skips
open_points.text: M19 says a run is `succeeded` “when every node and output concluded successfully,” while the carried rule permits a flow output not to be produced under a guard outcome and reports it `skipped_by_guard`. It does not say whether that skipped outcome counts as successful completion.
open_points.question: What final Run status results when all executable work succeeds but one or more nodes or flow outputs are `skipped_by_guard`?
options: `succeeded`, with skipped nodes and outputs treated as valid conclusions
Another non-final or final status must represent a valid partial result
open_points.default_guess: Mark the run `succeeded`, treating guard-authorized skips as valid conclusions.
